# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book follows the path from RISC-V fundamentals to the implementation of a system-on-chip on FPGA and in an ASIC flow. CORE-V Wally serves as the main case study, alongside other open-source RISC-V architectures.

The [Introduction](intro.qmd) offers a Foundations Route, a Complete SoC Route and an ASIC Design Route for students, instructors and independent engineers. The [learning-path guide](learning-paths.qmd) identifies essential versus advanced activities and their compute budgets. A separate [coursework adoption](appendices/hsd-coursework.qmd) preserves the twelve-week, 6 ECTS Hardware System Design plan, its RA5–RA8 outcomes and assessment proposals.

Technical chapters develop their topics through three levels:

1. **Concepts** explains the foundations independently of a particular tool or implementation.
2. **Implementation** connects those foundations to SystemVerilog examples and real designs, especially CORE-V Wally.
3. **Hands-on Experiments** provides a plan for reproducible simulation, verification, synthesis, or performance experiments.

The chapters develop reusable RTL, SoC interfaces, verification, FPGA implementation, ASIC implementation, and selected advanced topics. The [final project review](summary.qmd) brings those topics together through expected evidence and individual defence questions. Experiment instructions state their prerequisites; rendering the book does not run the hardware toolchains.

The [complete case study](appendices/complete-case-study.qmd) follows the same dot-product accelerator through that journey with a common source/configuration manifest: independent/formal checks, real Wally firmware, FPGA placement/routing, ASIC GDSII, physical visuals and an engineering decision based on the extracted results. It separates simulated SoC integration from the physically implemented IP boundary and retains failed or unexecuted obligations.

The [repository README](https://github.com/antoniofloresgil/FromConceptToSiliconBook#download-and-prepare-the-environment) explains downloading the source, preparing the environment, building HTML/PDF and running the reference practices. Detailed and guided recipes are collected in @sec-reproducible-labs.
